اختتمت وزارة الدفاع مشاركتها في فعاليات "مخيم الأمين – فرجان دبي" الصيفي 2026، الذي نظمته "فرجان دبي" بالتعاون مع خدمة "الأمين" وهيئة تنمية المجتمع، وذلك في مقر "مدارس دبي"، في إطار دعم المبادرات الوطنية الهادفة إلى تنمية قدرات الشباب. واستقبل سعادة خليفة راشد الهاملي، مدير مكتب سمو وزير الدفاع، كلاً من معالي حصة بنت عيسى بوحميد، مدير عام هيئة تنمية المجتمع، ومعالي عائشة ميران، مدير عام هيئة المعرفة والتنمية البشرية بدبي، وسعادة مشعل جلفار، المدير التنفيذي لخدمات الإسعاف بدبي، وسعادة العميد عمر الفلاسي، المشرف على خدمة الأمين، خلال حفل تكريم المشاركين في مخيم "الأمين – فرجان دبي"، حيث اطلعوا على مخرجات البرامج والأنشطة التي قدمتها وزارة الدفاع ضمن المخيم، وما تضمنته من ورش عمل وفعاليات تفاعلية أسهمت في تنمية مهارات الطلبة وتعزيز وعيهم. وشملت مشاركة وزارة الدفاع تقديم محاضرات توعوية حول الخدمة الوطنية والاحتياطية، ومفاهيم الدفاع الجوي، إلى جانب تنفيذ ورش عمل تدريبية وتفاعلية في مدارس دبي بمدرسة البرشاء ومدرسة الخوانيج، كما أشرف مكتب سمو وزير الدفاع على تدريب عدد من طلاب المخيم ضمن برنامج عملي وتدريبي يهدف إلى تنمية مهاراتهم وتعزيز قيم الانضباط والعمل الجماعي. وتأتي هذه المشاركة في إطار حرص وزارة الدفاع على دعم المبادرات الوطنية وترسيخ قيم الانتماء والهوية الوطنية لدى الأجيال الناشئة، وتعزيز التعاون مع مختلف الجهات الحكومية والمؤسسات المجتمعية، في إعداد جيلٍ واعٍ ومسؤول يسهم في مسيرة التنمية المستدامة في دولة الإمارات. #وزارة_الدفاع #وزارة_الدفاع_الإماراتية #MOD #UAEMinistryOfDefence

COGAT's Statement Regarding the IPC Report: COGAT strongly rejects the claims and conclusions presented in the IPC report. Time and again, IPC reports have been shown to rely on flawed methodology, incomplete sources of information, and systematic bias. As such, they do not constitute a professional or objective basis for assessing the humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip. The authors of the report did not contact COGAT prior to publishing their conclusions. In fact, in all their recent reports they repeatedly chose to disregard the data and information made available to them by COGAT. This conduct demonstrates that the current report is not the product of a genuine professional effort to assess the humanitarian reality, but rather an attempt to justify a predetermined narrative while systematically ignoring facts that contradict it, thereby serving Hamas propaganda and defaming the State of Israel. Approximately two weeks ago, COGAT published a comprehensive report based on data from the United Nations, international organizations, the CMCC, and other verified sources, presenting a transparent and comprehensive assessment of the humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip. The report's findings demonstrate unequivocally that the humanitarian situation remained stable and improved throughout the ceasefire period. Since the beginning of the ceasefire, approximately 1.8 million tons of food have entered the Gaza Strip, nearly three times the requirements defined by the World Food Programme (WFP). The substantial volume of food and its variety entering the Gaza Strip has significantly improved food availability in local markets and contributed to an approximately 72% decline in food prices. In the field of water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), more than 70,000 cubic meters of water are supplied to the Gaza Strip every day, significantly exceeding international humanitarian standards. At the same time, Israel continues to facilitate the entry of extensive water, sanitation and hygiene equipment, coordinate ongoing repairs to water infrastructure, approve new waste collection sites, and advance requests and projects submitted by international organizations. In the medical sector, more than 18,000 tons of medicines and medical supplies, including advanced and sensitive medical equipment, have entered the Gaza Strip since the ceasefire began. As a result, the number of hospitals and medical facilities operating in Gaza has increased significantly, while hospital bed capacity has expanded by 55%. These facts reflect Israel's continued commitment to expanding the humanitarian response in the Gaza Strip. Those who choose to ignore these facts divert attention from the primary obstacle to improving the humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip: the Hamas terrorist organization, which continues to seize humanitarian aid, exploit the humanitarian space for its military and governing purposes, and refuse to disarm. This conduct has also been condemned by UN officials, who have pointed to Hamas's interference in humanitarian operations and its repeated attempts to disrupt them. COGAT will continue to work together with the United States, the United Nations, and its international partners to expand the humanitarian response for the civilian population in the Gaza Strip while safeguarding Israel's security interests and preventing the exploitation of humanitarian assistance by the Hamas terrorist organization. Current information on the humanitarian state in Gaza can be found in COGAT’s humanitarian situation report. To read the Humanitarian Situation Report: http://bit.ly/4p8iCOp

💧 COGAT continues to support and coordinate WASH solutions for the civilian population of the Gaza Strip. Just this week, we published a notice to the civilian population regarding water availability, encouraging them to report areas experiencing water shortages. We received numerous responses from them, and accordingly, we coordinated the dispatch of water tankers to those specific locations in collaboration with the international community and local stakeholders. Furthermore, we have approved 10 major WASH-related requests, in alignment with projects submitted by the international community, aimed at strengthening the WASH infrastructure within the Strip. These requests include dual-use equipment that was approved under the special oversight mechanism in coordination with the international community, aimed at preventing Hamas from seizing the aid. This serves as proof that there is no blanket ban on the entry of dual-use equipment.

Earlier today, IDF soldiers operating in the Security Zone in southern Lebanon identified Lebanese Armed Forces personnel, accompanied by an engineering vehicle, who crossed ~150 meters into the Security Zone and breached barriers in the area of Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, contrary to the understandings between the parties. IDF soldiers operating in the area fired warning shots into the air only, which did not endanger the Lebanese Armed Forces personnel, in order to distance them from the area. The Lebanese Armed Forces personnel withdrew from the area, and no injuries were reported. The area into which the Lebanese Armed Forces entered is not part of the “pilot” area. The IDF calls on the Lebanese Armed Forces to continue operating in accordance with the understandings and within the agreed areas. Any deviation from these areas without prior coordination could endanger its forces.

Yesterday, due to COGAT’s coordinative efforts in full cooperation with the international community, 80 Gazans were evacuated from Gaza. Leaving from the Kerem Shalom Crossing to the Allenby Border Crossing into Jordan, these civilians left for multiple third countries based on their dual citizenship, visas for third countries, or for coordinated medical treatment. A significant part of this group consisted of children with cancer who will receive life-saving medical treatment in a third country. Coordinated by the American Embassy in Israel with COGAT, 26 Gazan children and their escorts left the Gaza Strip to head toward Jordan and then fly to their respective host country from there. In addition, the Rafah Border Crossing has remained operational. To date, roughly 4,800 people have entered, and 5,000 have exited Gaza via the border crossing.
